scope: Synthetic single-host model; no proprietary HyperFeed code or measured production mix
Identical phased trace, full returned rows and per-phase state/output parity against serial reference
One process per worker, rotating assignments; distinct events ordered per family, duplicate deliveries compete
128 preallocated typed slots/family; native guards before Aerostore snapshot, PostgreSQL FOR UPDATE at transaction start
Aerostore direct shared memory vs PostgreSQL local client/server; not equal transport overhead
WAL enabled, asynchronous acknowledgement in both; clean WAL drain checked, crash durability untested
Native contract probes supply no predicate lock and determine overall compatibility status
No speedup claim: rates include process dispatch/barriers and bounded fixture coordination

cases.name: serializable_absent_candidate_creation
cases.details: Expected one commit and one serialization rejection when two overlapping transactions both find no matching flight and activate different slots for the same key. Observed initial candidate counts=0/0, committed=2, rejected=0, matching_rows=2, matching_index_postings=2. Both writers held their own native indexed-row guard; no predicate lock was added.

cases.name: committed_row_and_index_visibility
cases.details: Expected a successfully committed reader to find a newly committed row through its new index key. Paused the writer between native row commit and index maintenance while retaining its indexed-row guard. Observed visible_row=Some(20), new_key_candidates=[], reader_committed=true; after index publication candidates=[0].

cases.name: index_candidates_respect_transaction_snapshot
cases.details: Expected the native transaction snapshot's old-key row to remain discoverable after another transaction moves that row's key, or the candidate reader to reject its transaction. An independent equally old snapshot sees row=Some(10); old_key_candidates=[], candidate_reader_committed=true. This checks fixed-snapshot candidate completeness, not just latest-state index consistency.

cases.name: savepoint_and_whole_message_rollback
cases.details: Expected rollback to preserve pre-savepoint multirow writes [90,60,0], discard nested candidate writes, and leave the committed transfer unchanged after a later whole-message abort. Observed restored=[Some(90), Some(60), Some(0)], committed=true, committed_rows=[(0, 90), (1, 60), (2, 0)], after_abort=[(0, 90), (1, 60), (2, 0)]. This probe covers native table state; it makes no claim about an external index overlay.

cases.name: multirow_table_snapshot_visibility
cases.details: Expected a reader spanning a two-row transfer to retain [100,50] in its snapshot, and a new reader to observe [90,60]. Observed old_reader=[Some(100),Some(50)], writer_committed=true, new_reader=[Some(90), Some(60)], new_reader_committed=true. Both views must conserve total=150.

cases.name: concrete_read_dependency_write_skew
cases.details: Expected one serialization rejection when overlapping transactions read both active records and each deactivates a different record. Observed committed=1, rejected=1, remaining_active=1, final_rows=[(0, 0), (1, 1)]. This contrasts concrete row-read dependencies with the separate empty-candidate probe.

cases.name: serializable_absent_candidate_creation
cases.details: PostgreSQL SERIALIZABLE: overlapping absent-key searches returned 0/0; committed=1, rejected=1, matching_rows=1. Expected exactly one surviving flight; the other transaction must fail with SQLSTATE 40001/40P01.

cases.name: committed_row_and_index_visibility
cases.details: PostgreSQL publishes rows and indexes in one transaction: before COMMIT row_key=10, new-key candidates=0; after COMMIT row_key=20, new-key candidates=1. Expected 10/0 then 20/1; no externally split index maintenance exists.

cases.name: index_candidates_respect_transaction_snapshot
cases.details: PostgreSQL fixed snapshot started before a committed key move: visible_row_key=10, old-key candidates=1, reader_committed=true. Expected the old row to remain discoverable or transaction rejection.

cases.name: savepoint_and_whole_message_rollback
cases.details: PostgreSQL nested savepoint rollback restored=[90, 60, 0]; committed values after subsequent whole-message abort=[90, 60, 0]. Expected [90,60,0] in both observations.

cases.name: multirow_table_snapshot_visibility
cases.details: PostgreSQL old reader spanning a two-row transfer observed [100,50]; new reader observed [90, 60]. Expected [100,50] and [90,60], both conserving 150.

cases.name: concrete_read_dependency_write_skew
cases.details: PostgreSQL overlapping transactions read both active records then deactivate different records: committed=1, rejected=1, remaining_active=1. Expected one serialization rejection and one remaining record.
